newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Boutros-Ghali raps Savimbi for boycotting meeting.
newsitem.headline: Boutros-Ghali raps Savimbi for boycotting meeting.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali on Wednesday rapped Angolan leader Jonas Savimbi for boycotting a summit that South African President Nelson Mandela and others hoped would bring peace.
Savimbi, head of the former rebel National Union for the Total Independence of Angola or UNITA, failed to come to the government-held capital of Luanda from his stronghold in Bailundo in the north.
"The secretary-General is very disappointed as he had been in communication with Dr Savimbia several times," said spokeswoman Sylvana Foa.
"His presence would have helped accelerate implementation of the peace accords signed in 1994. But unfortunately he failed to show up," she said.
The meeting was called by the 12-nation Southern African Development Community and included heads of state from Zimbabwe, Namibia, Mozambique, Zambia and Botswana as well as South Africa,

President Frederick Chiluba of Zambia had invited Savimbi to join his arch rival, Angolan President Eduardo dos Santos, at the summit in an effort to jump-start Angola's troubled two-year-old peace process.
Without him the effectiveness of the meeting, the first of its kind, will be limited.
The United Nations has a 7,200-member peacekeeping operation mission in Angola, its largest remaining mission.
It is helping implement the agreement signed in Lusaka, Zambia, in November 1994, ending nearly two decades of civil war between the Angolan government and UNITA.
